description: The official NWS wind chill formula (35.74 + 0.6215T − 35.75V^0.16 + 0.4275TV^0.16) with °C/km/h input support and validity warnings.

faqs.a: WC = 35.74 + 0.6215T − 35.75(V^0.16) + 0.4275T(V^0.16), with T in °F and V in mph. It is only valid for temperatures at or below 50°F (10°C) and wind speeds of 3 mph (4.8 km/h) or more.
faqs.q: What is the wind chill formula?

faqs.a: Wind does not make the air colder — it strips away the thin insulating layer of warm air around exposed skin, so the body loses heat faster and skin feels (and gets) colder.
faqs.q: Does wind actually lower the temperature?

faqs.a: The tool warns you when inputs are outside the formula's valid range. Below a −18°F (−28°C) wind chill, exposed skin can freeze in 30 minutes or less.

Read the wind chill plus a frostbite warning when it is dangerously cold.
